properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECB selectable as options.mode in the wallet's AES wrapper (walletCrypto/utils.js) — ECB leaks plaintext structure block-by-block; no call site in this package passes AES.ECB, but the wrapper exposes it to every caller, and reachability through callers is exactly why the mode is inventoried. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Declared dependency: crypto-js@3.3.0 pinned in yarn.lock — ships MD5, SHA-1, SHA-2, HMAC, AES, DES, RC4-drop, Rabbit, PBKDF2 to the bundle. Version 3.3.0 is a 2015-era release predating the crypto-js 4.x fixes (weak hash defaults, RC4/RC4Drop MD5-based RNG issues). Presence in the lockfile is the inventory question; what the app actually calls matters for urgency but not for keeping the entry. Changeable by bumping the dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Default cipher mode of the wallet's own AES wrapper (walletCrypto/utils.js): encrypt/decrypt call crypto.createCipheriv(options.mode || AES.CBC, key, salt || '') — unauthenticated CBC is the default path for wallet payload encryption, and the IV is the caller-supplied salt (empty string when salt is null). Changeable here: the wrapper should move to AES-256-GCM (already defined in the same map) or add an HMAC.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 (Ethereum's pre-FIPS-202 padding variant, via ethers.utils.keccak256) used for NFT order/signature hashing in the Wyvern exchange utils. The hash itself is fine cryptographically; its use is protocol-mandated by Ethereum contracts — replaceable only by the chain, observable here. Not a vulnerability driver on its own; recorded because the order-hash scheme would need a chain-level migration if Ethereum ever moves off keccak.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The wallet's AES wrapper runs AES with 256-bit keys in every mode it exposes (CBC default, ECB, GCM, OFB) — key size is the strong part of this asset; the mode-specific weaknesses are tracked on the CBC/ECB/OFB objects. Quantum margin is fine; no change needed for key size.
